name: Ragú Napoletano (Neapolitan-Style Italian Meat Sauce With Pork, Beef, and Sausage)

ingredients.name: mild Italian sausage, in the casings

instructions.primary_message: Cut the pork spare ribs into 2 chunks. Cut the boneless beef chuck into 2 chunks. Cut the boneless pork shoulder into 2 chunks. Finely chop the yellow onion.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.9 kg pork spare ribs
0.9 kg boneless beef chuck
0.9 kg boneless pork shoulder
1 large yellow onion

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position and preheat oven to 150°C (300°F). Season ribs with salt and pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven over high heat until shimmering. Add ribs and cook without moving until well browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Flip and cook until second side is well browned, 5 to 7 minutes longer. Transfer to a plate and set aside. Repeat with beef chuck and pork shoulder until browned all over and add to plate with pork ribs.

Add onions to now-empty Dutch oven and cook, scraping up any browned bits, and stirring frequently until lightly browned, about 8 minutes. Add tomato paste, and cook, stirring often, until paste begins to caramelize, about 2 minutes. Add wine and cook until mixture is very thick, about 5 minutes. Add tomatoes, Parmesan rind (if using), and 3/4 of basil. Return ribs, beef chuck, and pork shoulder to pot and bring to a simmer.

Cover with lid slightly ajar and place in the oven (see notes for slow cooker instructions). Cook, stirring occasionally, until the rib bones can be easily pulled from the meat, about 3 hours. Add sausages and continue cooking for 30 minutes. Remove from oven and reduce oven temperature to 93°C (200°F).

Transfer pork ribs, beef chuck, pork shoulder, and sausages to a bowl, discard bones, and let stand until cool enough to handle. Discard basil sprigs from sauce. Arrange meat on a platter, pour 1/2 cup tomato sauce over meat, cover with aluminum foil, and keep warm in oven while sauce reduces.

Bring the tomato sauce in the Dutch oven to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring often, until sauce has thickened, developed a deep red color, and reduced to about 4 cups, about 1 hour. Stir in remaining olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

To serve, cook pasta in a pot of boiling salted water until just shy of al dente (about 1 minute for fresh pasta or 1 minute short of recommended cooking time for dried pasta). Drain, reserving about 1 cup of starchy pasta water. Return pasta to the pot you just cooked it in and add half of ragù, half of pasta cooking water, and a handful of grated cheese. Cook over medium-high heat, stirring until the sauce emulsifies with the pasta water and clings to the pasta, adding more pasta water if necessary. Serve immediately, passing additional sauce, cheese, and remaining fresh basil at the table. Carve and serve meat either alongside pasta or as the following course.

schema_metadata.keywords: beef, Italian, italian american, Naples, pasta, pork, ragu, sauce

description: Ragù Napoletano is a meaty stew featuring big chunks of beef, pork, and sausages simmered until fall-apart tender in a deep and rich tomato sauce.
notes:
Optional or for serving: 1 (5 to 8-cm) Parmesan rind (optional); Grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, for serving

Optional substitutions: yellow onion → red onion; fresh pasta → dried pasta

Notes: Any mildly flavored sausage from the butcher will do. If no mild sausages are available, sweet Italian sausages will work.
author: J. Kenji López-Alt
